newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat holds talks in Egypt on peace process.
newsitem.headline: Arafat holds talks in Egypt on peace process.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held a second day of talks in Egypt on Thursday on ways to break the deadlock in the Middle East peace process.

He met Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who said in remarks published on Thursday that Israel had created the current crisis in the Middle East peace process by wanting to impose a "right-wing, Likud" vision of peace.

"The obstacles we face now, or those faced by the peace process, can be summarised in one sentence: The current Israeli policies want to impose an Israeli peace, a Likud and rightwing peace," Moussa said in an interview in al-Ahram daily.
"It can neither be borne nor accepted. It will lead to the collapse of the foundations of peace itself," Moussa said.
Moussa and Arafat had held talks on Wednesday on the stalemate in the Middle East peace process. Arafat also met with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak during his visit to Cairo.

The two leaders consult often on the Middle East peace process, which has been stalled since Israel started building on March 18 a new 6,500-home Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in 1967 and later annexed.
On March 21, a Palestinian militant opposed to peace killed himself and three Israelis in a Tel Aviv cafe bombing.
Mubarak and Israeli President Ezer Weizman plan to meet soon to try and salvage Israeli-PLO peace talks.
Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its undivided capital. Palestinians want the eastern part to be the capital of their future state.
Palestinians see Jewish settlement-building as pre-empting "final status" peace talks which have yet to resume since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took power last June.
